984.1: Raag Mali Gaura, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace. (Beings) have worn themselves out with countless efforts, yet none has found the Lord's end. O Lord, you are beyond reach, beyond all reach, and the knowing of you is past fathoming; to you, Lord God, my King, I bow. Lust, anger, greed and attachment stir (beings) to strife, and they quarrel without end. Save us, save us, O Lord: we are your humble beggars; O Lord God, we have come to your refuge. O God, you cherish those who come to your refuge; O Lord, your Name is Bhagat Vachhal, the lover of devotion. Harnakhash seized your servant Prahlad, but you, O Lord, saved him and carried him across. Remember the Lord, O mind, to reach his mansion; the King is the destroyer of all sorrow. O Master, O Lord, take away the fear of birth and death; through the Guru's teaching God is found. The Name of the Lord, the Master, purifies the fallen; those who have sung of him, the destroyer of his devotees' fear, and have set the garland of the Lord's Name upon their hearts, have merged in the Name, O servant Nanak. ॥4॥
Prahlad, son of the demon king Harnakhash (Hiranyakashipu), held to devotion to God through all his father's torments, and God saved him.
984.2: Raag Mali Gaura, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O mind, repeat the Name of Ram, the giver of peace. Joining the Sat Sangat (the company of the true), (one) has tasted the Lord's savour, and through the Guru has recognised Brahm, God. The fortunate one has had the sight of the Guru; when the Guru is met, the Lord God is known. All the filth of evil thinking has gone out (of him); he has bathed in the Lord's Amrit, in the Lord's pool. Blessed, blessed are the Saadhs (the holy) who have found the Lord God; I ask them to tell me of the Lord. I fall at their feet and pray to them each day: in your grace unite me with the Lord, the Creator. By what was written on the forehead (one) has found the Guru, the Saadh; mind and body are dyed in the Guru's words. The Lord God has come and met him; he has found peace, and all sins and misdeeds are cast away. Those who through the Guru's teaching have found the elixir of Ram's Name, the home of all delights: theirs is the highest glory. The dust of their feet is found by great fortune; servant Nanak falls at their feet. ॥4॥
985.1: Raag Mali Gaura, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). All the Siddhas (yogis held to have reached perfection), the seekers and the silent sages have meditated on the Lord with devotion in their minds. The Supreme Lord (Paarbrahm), beyond the farthest beyond, the Master, the unseen Lord: the Guru has shown him (to them). We are lowly and have done base deeds; we have not remembered the Lord, the King. The Lord brought the True Guru and united (us with him), and in an instant (we) were freed from our bonds. The one on whose forehead God wrote it from the start has, through the Guru's teaching, fixed his loving attention on the Lord. In the Lord's court the five Shabads (sounds) have rung out; he has met the Lord and sung the song of joy. The Name of Narhari, the Lord, purifies the fallen, but it has not pleased the unfortunate. They are worn away in womb after womb of birth, as salt dissolves in water. O Lord, O God, O Master beyond reach, give me the understanding to keep my mind on the Guru's feet, that I may stay attached to the Name of the Lord, Ram, and, O servant Nanak, remain merged in the Name. ॥4॥
The five Shabads (sounds): the music of the five kinds of instrument (strings, metal, wind, skin drums and pots), an image of full joy.
985.2: Raag Mali Gaura, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). My mind is held by the Name of Ram, by its sweet relish. The lotus (of my heart) has blossomed, for I have found the Guru; I have repeated the Lord's Name, and doubt and fear have fled. My heart has taken to devotion, in awe and in love; through the Guru's teaching my sleeping mind has awoken. Sins have wasted away and peace has come; by great fortune I have enshrined the Lord in my heart. The manmukh (the self-willed) is the fleeting colour of kasumbh, like a flower that is fair for four days. In a moment it perishes; he suffers, and the punishment of Dharam Raj falls upon him. In the Sat Sangat, love for the Saadh, the Guru, grows very deep, as the dye of madder takes hold fast. Though the cloth of the body be torn into many rags, the blessed colour of the Lord does not fade. On one who meets the Guru the Lord's colour is laid, and glory is his; he is dyed in the Lord's deep crimson. Servant Nanak washes the feet of every servant who is attached to the Lord's feet. ॥4॥
Kasumbh, the safflower, gives a bright dye that soon fades. Madder (majith): a red dye from the root of a plant, a colour that never fades. Dharam Raj judges each soul by its deeds.
985.3: Raag Mali Gaura, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O my mind, worship with love the Name of the Lord, Har Har, Gopal (the Lord who sustains all). My mind and body are absorbed in the Name of Ram; through the Guru's teaching my understanding (has found) Ram, the home of all delights. Through the Guru's teaching let us meditate on the Name of the Lord, Har Har, and in the mind tell the rosary of the Lord's Name. Those on whose foreheads it is written have met the Lord, the Lord of the forest garland. Those who have meditated on the Lord's Name: all their entanglements are at an end. Jam (the messenger of Death) does not come near them; the Guru has saved them, and the Lord is their protector. We are children and know nothing; the Lord, our mother and father, cherishes (us). Ever we put our hands into the fire of Maya (the world's illusion and lure), but the Guru, merciful to the meek, has saved (us). The one who was most filthy has become pure; the Lord's praise has burnt away all sins. Bliss has come into the mind of the one who has found the Guru; O servant Nanak, through the Shabad he is filled with delight. ॥4॥
985.4: Raag Mali Gaura, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O my mind, worship with love the Lord, who cuts away all sins. The Perfect Guru has enshrined the Lord, Har Har, in (my) heart; may my head be laid down on the Guru's path. Whoever tells me of my Lord God, to him I would give my mind, cut into pieces. The Perfect Guru has united me with my Friend, the Lord; through the Guru's word I am sold in every market. (One) has given much in charity at Prayag at Makar; (one) has given up his body, cut in two; yet without the Lord's Name no one attains liberation, though much gold be cut into pieces and given away. The one who through the Guru's teaching has sung the Lord's praise, his glory: the shut doors of his mind have opened. With the knitted brow (trikuti, the mind's fretting) broken, doubt and fear have fled; the pot, the jar of worldly shame, is shattered. In Kalyug, those on whose foreheads it was written from the start have found the Perfect Guru. O servant Nanak, they have drunk the relish of Amrit, and all their hunger and thirst is gone.

Makar: the first of Magh, when the sun enters Capricorn; a bath and gifts at Prayag on that day were held to bring great merit. Some had their bodies sawn by the karvat (saw) at Kashi in the hope of liberation. Chhaka 1: the first set of six shabads; the count is written after the shabad's numbers.
986.1: Raag Mali Gaura, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O mind, service of the Lord is the most excellent peace. All other services are false; (for them) Jam strikes ever at the head. Those on whose foreheads it is written have come to join the Sangat. The Sants of the Lord, the infinite Being, have carried (them) across the terrifying ocean of the world. Serve every day the feet of the Saadh, the Guru, giving up greed, attachment and vice. Give up every hope in another; keep your hope in the One, the Formless Lord. Some, the Saakats (those who have turned from God), stray, lost in doubt; without the Guru (they are) in pitch darkness. What was to be from the start has come to pass; no one can erase it. The form of Gobind (the Lord of the universe) is beyond reach; the infinite Lord has countless Names. Blessed, blessed are those people, O Nanak, who have enshrined the Lord's Name in their hearts. ॥4॥
986.2: Raag Mali Gaura, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Salutation to the Name of Ram, repeating which, one is saved. By remembering him, worldly entanglements are ended; by remembering him, bonds are broken; by remembering him, fools become wise; by remembering him, whole families are saved. By remembering him, (one) is rid of fear and sorrow; by remembering him, misfortune is turned away; by remembering him, sins are done away; by remembering him, no anguish remains. By remembering him, the heart blossoms; by remembering him, Kavla (Lakshmi, Maya) becomes a handmaid; by remembering him, (one gains) all treasures and storehouses; by remembering him, (beings) cross over in the end. The Lord's Name purifies the fallen; it saves millions of devotees. The humble one (Nanak) is in the refuge of the servants of the Lord's servants; Nanak's forehead rests on the feet of the Sants. ॥4॥
986.3: Raag Mali Gaura, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Such a helper is the Lord's Name: worship it with love in the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy), and every purpose is fulfilled. As a boat comes to one who is drowning, as oil comes to a lamp going out, as water comes to one burning in fire, as milk to the mouth of a child; as a brother stands by one in battle, as food alone (helps) the hungry, as rain from the clouds to the crops, as protection in the refuge of a lion; (as) with Garur (the antidote) in the mouth there is no fear of the snake, (as) the parrot in its cage is safe from the cat, as the egg (is kept safe) in the heart (of the crane), as grains (are spared) at the hub of the millstone. The likenesses are many; I have told only a few. O Lord, you alone are beyond reach, beyond all reach, unfathomable; (you are) lofty, great, utterly infinite. O Nanak, remembering (the Name), even those (heavy) as iron have crossed over. ॥4॥

Garur: a remedy against snake venom, named after Garuda, the bird who is the enemy of snakes; it was ground on a stone and taken by mouth. By tradition the crane flies far from her eggs and keeps them alive by holding them in her mind. Grains that stay by the pivot of the mill are not ground between the stones.
987.1: Raag Mali Gaura, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). This alone is the fulfilment of my purpose: (O God,) be gracious to your own servant. my forehead (at) the feet of the Sants, with my eyes may I behold their sight night and day, my hands (be) in the service of the Sants, my breath of life, my mind and my wealth (given) to the Sants. My mind's love (be) for the company of the Sants; may the Sants' virtues dwell in my mind; the Sants' bidding (be) sweet to my mind; may my lotus (heart) blossom at the sight of the Sants. May my dwelling be in the company of the Sants; I have a great thirst for the Sants; the Sants' words (be) my mind's mantra; by the Sants' grace may my sinful passions be destroyed. This is the way to liberation, this the treasure: O merciful God, give me this gift. O God, show mercy to Nanak: may the feet of the Sants (dwell) within my heart. ॥4॥
987.2: Raag Mali Gaura, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (God) is with all, not far; he does and causes all to be done, ever present before us. Hearing his Name, one comes to life; sorrows are destroyed, and peace makes its home; the Lord, Har Har Hare, is all treasures; the silent sages serve him. In whose house all things are held, from whose door no one (turns away) empty, who cherishes all beings and creatures: serve that merciful Lord for ever and ever. In whose court there is always justice, who depends on none and is beholden to no one, who himself does all that is done: O my mind, repeat his Name. I am a sacrifice to the Saadh Sangat, meeting which, one is saved. Mind and body are dyed with the Name: God has granted this gift to Nanak. ॥4॥
987.3: Raag Mali Gaura, Dupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. (I have taken) the refuge of the all-powerful Lord; my soul, my body, my wealth, my capital: (all is) the One God, the root of all creation. Remembering him again and again, lasting peace is found; he is the root of life. He pervades every place, the subtle and the gross. Giving up the snares of the household and all vices, sing the Lord's virtues every day. With palms joined, Nanak begs this gift: give (me) your Name. ॥2॥
988.1: Raag Mali Gaura, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O God, all-powerful, infinite Divine Lord, who can know your wonders? They have no end and no far shore. In an instant he sets up and pulls down; he is the Maker who shapes and breaks. To all the creation he has made, God, the Giver, gives his gifts. Your servant has come to your refuge, O Lord, O God, lofty, beyond reach, Murari; pull him out of the treacherous world-ocean; servant Nanak is ever a sacrifice (to you). ॥2॥
Murari (the foe of the demon Mur): a name of God.
988.2: Raag Mali Gaura, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O Gopal, you dwell in (my) mind and body, friend of the poor, lover of devotion, merciful for ever and ever. In the beginning, the end and the middle, you alone are; without God there is no other. He fills all the worlds, the one Master alone. With my ears (I hear) the Lord's praise, with my eyes (I behold) his sight, with my tongue I sing the Lord's virtues. Nanak is ever a sacrifice: give (me) your Name. ॥2॥
988.3: Raag Mali Gaura, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Blessed, blessed is that flute of Ram, which is playing; its sweet, sweet melody resounds unbroken. Blessed, blessed is the fleece of the sheep; blessed, blessed the blanket that Krishna wears. Blessed, blessed are you, mother Devki, in whose house (was born) the beautiful Lord, Ramaiya, the husband of Kavla. Blessed, blessed are the forests of Brindaban, where Sri Narayan plays. He plays the flute and grazes the cows; Nama's Master revels in joy. ॥4॥
Namdev calls blessed all that belongs to the Lord in his form as Krishna: the flute, the woollen blanket, his mother Devki and the forests of Brindaban, where he played and grazed the cows.
988.4: O Madho, you are my father; blessed are you, O Keshav, O dark-hued one, O Bithal. Discus in hand, you came from Baikunth (heaven) and saved the life of Gaj, the elephant; in Duhsasan's court, as Dropati's clothes were being taken from her, you saved (her honour). You carried across Ahalya, Gotam's wife; many others too you have made pure and carried across. So lowly, of low caste, Namdev has come to your refuge. ॥2॥

Madho (maa, Maya or Lakshmi, and dhav, husband), Keshav (of the beautiful hair) and Bithal (Sanskrit Vitthala) are names of Vishnu and Krishna in the Puranas; for Namdev they are names of the one God. Gaj: in the Bhagavat Purana, an elephant seized in the water by a crocodile; when his strength failed he called on the Lord and was set free. Dropati (Draupadi): in the Mahabharata, the wife of the Pandavas, whom Duhsasan sought to strip in the court of the Kauravas, but her cloth did not run out. Ahalya: the wife of the sage Gotam, turned to stone by his curse and, in the Ramayana, set free at the touch of Ram.
988.5: In every heart Ram speaks; Ram alone speaks: who but Ram speaks, O brother? Of the one clay are the elephant and the ant: its vessels are many, of many kinds, O brother. The unmoving and the moving, worms and moths: in every heart Ram is contained, O brother. Keep your thought on the One, the Infinite; give up all other hopes, O brother. Nama humbly prays: for those who have become free of desire, who is the Master and who the servant, O brother? ॥2॥

(I have taken) the refuge of the all-powerful Lord;
my soul, my body, my wealth, my capital: (all is) the One God, the root of all creation.
Remembering him again and again, lasting peace is found; he is the root of life.
He pervades every place, the subtle and the gross.
Giving up the snares of the household and all vices, sing the Lord's virtues every day.
With palms joined, Nanak begs this gift: give (me) your Name. ॥2॥
988.1: Raag Mali Gaura, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O God, all-powerful, infinite Divine Lord,
who can know your wonders? They have no end and no far shore.
In an instant he sets up and pulls down; he is the Maker who shapes and breaks.
To all the creation he has made, God, the Giver, gives his gifts.
Your servant has come to your refuge, O Lord, O God, lofty, beyond reach, Murari;
pull him out of the treacherous world-ocean; servant Nanak is ever a sacrifice (to you). ॥2॥
988.2: Raag Mali Gaura, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Gopal, you dwell in (my) mind and body,
friend of the poor, lover of devotion, merciful for ever and ever.
In the beginning, the end and the middle, you alone are; without God there is no other.
He fills all the worlds, the one Master alone.
With my ears (I hear) the Lord's praise, with my eyes (I behold) his sight, with my tongue I sing the Lord's virtues.
Nanak is ever a sacrifice: give (me) your Name. ॥2॥
988.3: Raag Mali Gaura, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Blessed, blessed is that flute of Ram, which is playing;
its sweet, sweet melody resounds unbroken.
Blessed, blessed is the fleece of the sheep;
blessed, blessed the blanket that Krishna wears.
Blessed, blessed are you, mother Devki,
in whose house (was born) the beautiful Lord, Ramaiya, the husband of Kavla.
Blessed, blessed are the forests of Brindaban,
He plays the flute and grazes the cows;
988.4: O Madho, you are my father; blessed are you, O Keshav, O dark-hued one, O Bithal.
Discus in hand, you came from Baikunth (heaven) and saved the life of Gaj, the elephant;
in Duhsasan's court, as Dropati's clothes were being taken from her, you saved (her honour).
You carried across Ahalya, Gotam's wife; many others too you have made pure and carried across.
So lowly, of low caste, Namdev has come to your refuge. ॥2॥
988.5: In every heart Ram speaks; Ram alone speaks:
who but Ram speaks, O brother?
Of the one clay are the elephant and the ant: its vessels are many, of many kinds, O brother.
The unmoving and the moving, worms and moths: in every heart Ram is contained, O brother.
Keep your thought on the One, the Infinite; give up all other hopes, O brother.
Nama humbly prays: for those who have become free of desire, who is the Master and who the servant, O brother? ॥2॥
